name: Gardens of Golden Gate Park
description: The Gardens of Golden Gate Park include the Conservatory of Flowers (the oldest public wood-and-glass conservatory in North America), the Japanese Tea Garden (the oldest operating public Japanese garden in North America), and the San Francisco Botanical Garden (55 acres with more than 8,000 kinds of plants).
fullDescription: The Gardens of Golden Gate Park include the Conservatory of Flowers (the oldest public wood-and-glass conservatory in North America), the Japanese Tea Garden (the oldest operating public Japanese garden in North America), and the San Francisco Botanical Garden (55 acres with more than 8,000 kinds of plants).
whatTheyOffer:
- Free for San Francisco residents and veterans at all three gardens
- Museums for All: Free general admission with an EBT card
- Botanical Garden: Free for everyone daily 7:30-9 a.m., on the second Tuesday of each month, and on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day
- Japanese Tea Garden: Free hour for everyone 9-10 a.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays
- Conservatory of Flowers: Free for everyone on the first Tuesday of the month (closed Wednesdays)
- Special exhibitions and events may cost extra
howToGetIt: Show proof of San Francisco residency, veteran ID, or your EBT card at the entrance. Anyone can visit free during the free hours and days listed above. Check the Admissions & Hours page for current hours, or call 415-661-1316.
